title: Coefficient biduality for inverse contravariant rational Weil data
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda=E$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ set $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Work in the rational bounded constructible categories with Weil pairs $(M,\theta_M:P_TM\simeq M)$ and Weil arrows $u\theta_M=\theta_NP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. All Weil isomorphisms below are arbitrary rational arrows; a Frobenius-stable integral lattice is not assumed.

Let $X_0$ be separated of finite type over $k_0$ and $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $(K,\theta_K)$ have site-perfect underlying bounded constructible complex [def-weil-site-perfect-complex]. Put $P=P_X$, $c:P\Lambda_X\simeq\Lambda_X$ for the canonical coefficient-unit datum [def-weil-frobenius-coefficient-twists], and $M^\vee=R\mathcal Hom_X(M,\Lambda_X)$. Use coefficient evaluation $\operatorname{ev}_M:M\otimes^LM^\vee\to\Lambda_X$, tensor symmetry $\sigma$, and tensor-Hom transposition. For $M=K,K^\vee$ the evaluation-defined comparison
$$h_M:PM^\vee\simeq R\mathcal Hom_X(PM,P\Lambda_X)$$
is the canonical comparison characterized by
$$\operatorname{ev}_{PM,P\Lambda_X}(1\otimes h_M)\mu=P(\operatorname{ev}_M),$$
where $\mu:P(U\otimes^LV)\simeq PU\otimes^LPV$ [lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation]. Give the two duals the inverse contravariant data
$$\theta_{K^\vee}=R\mathcal Hom_X(\theta_K^{-1},c)h_K,\qquad
\theta_{K^{\vee\vee}}=R\mathcal Hom_X(\theta_{K^\vee}^{-1},c)h_{K^\vee}.$$
The canonical coefficient bidual map
$$\delta_K:K\to K^{\vee\vee},\qquad
\delta_K=(\operatorname{ev}_K\sigma_{K^\vee,K})^\sharp$$
then satisfies
$$\delta_K\theta_K=\theta_{K^{\vee\vee}}P(\delta_K).$$
In particular it is the actual transpose of coefficient evaluation, with the symmetry and evaluation-defined comparisons retained, that is a Weil arrow. The assertion holds for arbitrary rational $\theta_K$, including $K=\Lambda_s$, $\theta_K=\ell$ on $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, and for the zero object.

proof.text: Write $A=K$, $B=K^\vee$, $C=K^{\vee\vee}$, $\alpha=\theta_K$, $\beta=\theta_{K^\vee}$ and $\gamma=\theta_{K^{\vee\vee}}$. The pairs $(K,\Lambda_X)$ and $(K^\vee,\Lambda_X)$ lie in the domain of the rational internal Hom because every pair of bounded constructible rational objects on the separated finite-type $k$-scheme $X$ does (the admissible Hom-substitution lemma, applied to $X$ viewed as a six-functor space); perfect-dual stability is not needed for this. The specified $h_A,h_B$ are isomorphisms. Since internal Hom is a bifunctor, $H(\alpha^{-1},c)$ and $H(\beta^{-1},c)$ are isomorphisms, with inverses $H(\alpha,c^{-1})$ and $H(\beta,c^{-1})$. Thus $\beta$ and $\gamma$ are isomorphisms in the rational category. Put $e_A=\operatorname{ev}_K$, $e_B=\operatorname{ev}_{K^\vee}$ and $t_{U,V}=\mu_{U,V}^{-1}:PU\otimes PV\to P(U\otimes V)$. All tensors below are derived tensors.

source.place: Final duality/pairing paragraph; explicit coefficient-bidual calculation supplementing the evaluation/transposition argument in cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance.proof.md, paragraph 2

proof.text:
For $M=A,B$ put $u=\theta_M$ and $v=\theta_{M^\vee}=H(u^{-1},c)h_M$. Naturality of the rational evaluation transpose gives
$$e_M(u\otimes v)=c\,\operatorname{ev}_{PM,P\Lambda_X}(1\otimes h_M).$$
Indeed the first-variable map in $H(u^{-1},c)$ composes an evaluated argument with $u^{-1}$, and the argument supplied here is $u$, so $u^{-1}u=1$; the second-variable map is $c$. The defining evaluation identity for $h_M$ now gives the two identities
$$e_A(\alpha\otimes\beta)=cP(e_A)t_{A,B},\qquad e_B(\beta\otimes\gamma)=cP(e_B)t_{B,C}.$$
These are equalities for arbitrary rational arrows by the cited rational transposition statement, rather than a calculation restricted to integral arrows.

source.place: Final duality/pairing paragraph; explicit coefficient-bidual calculation supplementing the evaluation/transposition argument in cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance.proof.md, paragraph 2

proof.text:
Set $b=e_A\sigma_{B,A}:B\otimes A\to\Lambda_X$ and $j=b^\sharp=\delta_K:A\to C$. By the evaluation formula for the bijective transpose,
$$e_B(1_B\otimes j)=b.$$
To prove $j\alpha=\gamma Pj$, it suffices by injectivity of that same transpose (with first variable $B$ and parameter $PA$) to compare $e_B(1_B\otimes j\alpha)$ and $e_B(1_B\otimes\gamma Pj)$, maps $B\otimes PA\to\Lambda_X$. Precomposition by the isomorphism $\beta\otimes1_{PA}:PB\otimes PA\to B\otimes PA$ is cancellable, so it suffices to compare their composites with this specified map.

source.place: Final duality/pairing paragraph; explicit coefficient-bidual calculation supplementing the evaluation/transposition argument in cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance.proof.md, paragraph 2

proof.text:
The first composite is
$$\begin{aligned}
e_B(\beta\otimes j\alpha)&=b(\beta\otimes\alpha)\\
&=e_A(\alpha\otimes\beta)\sigma_{PB,PA}\\
&=cP(e_A)t_{A,B}\sigma_{PB,PA}\\
&=cP(b)t_{B,A}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality is the defining transpose identity from step 3, the second is naturality of the prescribed rational signed symmetry, and the third is step 2. The last equality is precisely compatibility of the specified pullback-tensor comparison with that symmetry, namely $t_{A,B}\sigma_{PB,PA}=P(\sigma_{B,A})t_{B,A}$. Hence the cohomological signs are retained in this equality.

source.place: Final duality/pairing paragraph; explicit coefficient-bidual calculation supplementing the evaluation/transposition argument in cor-coef-verdier-weil-equivariance.proof.md, paragraph 2

proof.text:
The second composite is
$$\begin{aligned}
e_B(\beta\otimes\gamma Pj)&=e_B(\beta\otimes\gamma)(1_{PB}\otimes Pj)\\
&=cP(e_B)t_{B,C}(1_{PB}\otimes Pj)\\
&=cP(e_B)P(1_B\otimes j)t_{B,A}\\
&=cP(b)t_{B,A}.
\end{aligned}$$
The first equality is tensor functoriality; the second is the other evaluation identity of step 2; the third is naturality of $t$ for the actual rational arrow $j:A\to C$; and the fourth uses $e_B(1_B\otimes j)=b$ from step 3 and functoriality of $P$. Thus the two composites agree.

proof.text: Cancel $\beta\otimes1_{PA}$ in steps 4–5 and use the injective transpose of step 3. This gives $\delta_K\theta_K=\theta_{K^{\vee\vee}}P(\delta_K)$, which is exactly the defining Weil-arrow equation. Only rational inverses and rational naturality were used, so no stable integral lattice is required. On a point with $K=E$ and $\alpha=\ell$, the displayed dual formulas give $\beta=\ell^{-1}$ and $\gamma=\ell$, while $j$ is the usual evaluation identification, so the equation holds. At the zero object both compared maps are the unique zero morphism; no cancellation by a nonzero scalar was used.
